result: E2 treatment induces a transition in Kiss1ARH neurons from silent/tonic firing in ovariectomized (OVX) mice to bursting/irregular firing patterns, as demonstrated by whole-cell current-clamp recordings (Figure 1).
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the experimental data showing firing pattern changes but express concern that the OVX vs. OVX+E2 comparison 'may not reflect the physiological conditions under which the proposed transition...might take place (i.e. the diestrous [low E2] and proestrous [high E2] stages of the estrous cycle).' This is identified as 'an important caveat' that limits interpretation of the findings' physiological relevance.

result: Pharmacological dissection of voltage-activated calcium currents in Kiss1ARH neurons reveals that L-type (26.1%), N-type (25.1%), and R-type (31.1%) channels constitute the largest components, with smaller contributions from T-type (6.7%) and P/Q-type (3.9%) channels (Figure 2).
evaluation: Reviewers describe the 'pharmacological and electrophysiological experiments' as 'of the highest standards' and note that 'the authors add interesting information on the complement of ionic currents in ARC kisspeptin neurons.' No concerns are raised about these specific pharmacological characterization data.

result: Multiple voltage-activated calcium channel subtypes contribute to the NKB-mediated slow EPSP in Kiss1ARH neurons, with nifedipine, ω-conotoxin MVIIC, SNX-482, and TTA-P2 all significantly inhibiting the slow EPSP, and Cd2+ blocking the senktide-induced inward current (Figure 3).
evaluation: Reviewers note that the 'pharmacological and electrophysiological experiments appear of the highest standards' and that the data are 'compelling.' The experimental approach combining optogenetic stimulation with pharmacology is identified as a strength of the study.

result: E2 treatment upregulates mRNA expression of all voltage-activated calcium channel subtypes (Cacna1g, Cacna1e, Cacna1c, Cacna1b, Cacna1a) in Kiss1ARH neurons (Figure 4).
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledge 'the impact of E2 replacement on calcium and potassium currents is compelling,' they emphasize that 'E2 alters certain ionic currents when added back to OVX females, does not mean that the magnitude of all of these ionic currents will vary during the estrous cycle.' One reviewer notes confusion about whether the computational model was based on qPCR data or recordings, stating 'it is well known that post-translational modifications, physiological modulation of individual channel biophysical properties, and many other factors can influence the end output of a membrane conductance.'

result: E2 treatment significantly increases peak calcium current density in Kiss1ARH neurons without altering voltage dependence of activation or inactivation, indicating increased channel expression rather than altered kinetics (Figures 5-6).
evaluation: Reviewers state 'the impact of E2 replacement on calcium and potassium currents is compelling' and describe the experiments as having 'robust statistical analyses.' The combination of experimental data and computational modeling recapitulation is noted as a strength.

result: E2 treatment increases overall outward K+ current density in Kiss1ARH neurons, but the apamin-sensitive SK channel component remains unchanged, and SK3 (Kcnn3) mRNA expression is unaffected (Figure 7).
evaluation: Reviewers describe the pharmacological experiments as 'of the highest standards' with 'robust statistical analyses.' The characterization of potassium currents is part of the 'interesting information on the complement of ionic currents' that reviewers acknowledge.

result: E2 treatment significantly increases BK channel current and Kcnma1 (BKα1) mRNA expression in Kiss1ARH neurons, with iberiotoxin-sensitive current substantially larger in E2-treated females (Figure 8).
evaluation: Reviewers note 'the impact of E2 replacement on calcium and potassium currents is compelling' and describe the experiments as having 'robust statistical analyses provided throughout.' No specific concerns are raised about the BK channel data.

result: E2 treatment increases M-current (KCNQ) and Kv2.1 channel expression and function in Kiss1ARH neurons, with XE-991-sensitive current significantly elevated in E2-treated females and increased Kcnq2 and Kcnb1 mRNA expression (Figure 9).
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the 'robust statistical analyses' and describe the pharmacological experiments as 'of the highest standards.' The potassium channel characterization is part of the 'interesting information' on ionic currents that reviewers recognize.

result: E2 treatment produces reciprocal changes in gene expression in Kiss1ARH neurons: decreasing Tac2 (NKB), Trpc5, and Kcnj6 (GIRK) while increasing Slc17a6 (Vglut2) mRNA (Figure 10).
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledge the data quality, they express concern about physiological relevance, noting that 'E2 alters certain ionic currents when added back to OVX females, does not mean that the magnitude of all of these ionic currents will vary during the estrous cycle.' One reviewer specifically questions the assumption that 'conductance is directly proportional to the mRNA expression' and requests literature citation for this correlation.

result: CRISPR/SaCas9-mediated knockdown of Trpc5 in Kiss1ARH neurons eliminates the slow EPSP, hyperpolarizes resting membrane potential by 7 mV, increases rheobase by ~13%, and reduces firing frequency (Figures 11-12).
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge that 'the results of Trpc5 gene knockdown do provide good evidence that the TRPC5 channel plays a key role in mediating the NKB-mediated slow EPSP' and note the 'unsuspected role for this channel in regulating the membrane potential and excitability.' However, they express significant concern that 'CRISPR knockdown of the TRPC5 channel reduced overall excitability, but this was only examined in cells from ovariectomized mice without estradiol treatment' and that 'the results can only suggest that CRISPR-mediated knockdown of TRPC5 can, at best, phenocopy the OVX+E condition.' They recommend 'acknowledging this as a limitation.'

result: Computational modeling demonstrates that E2-induced changes in ionic conductances enable Kiss1ARH neurons to transition from TRPC5-dependent synchronous firing to burst firing driven by elevated h- and Ca2+ currents, with the balance between TRPC5 and GIRK conductances controlling neuronal excitability (Figures 12-13).
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge that 'the addition of computer simulations for understanding the impact of E2 on the electrical activity of ARC kisspeptin cells is also a strength.' However, they note a critical limitation: 'although the computational modeling indicates a role of the various E2-modulated conductances in causing a transition in ARC kisspeptin neuron firing pattern, their role is not directly tested in physiological recordings, weakening the link between these changes and the shift in firing patterns.' One reviewer expresses confusion about model parameterization, noting discrepancies in the methods description about whether qPCR data or recordings were used.

result: The authors propose that Kiss1ARH neurons transition from peptidergic neurotransmission driving pulsatile GnRH release in low E2 conditions to glutamatergic transmission facilitating the preovulatory GnRH surge in high E2 conditions through projections to Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state that 'some of the conclusions of the work, with regard, in particular, to the role of these changes in ion channels and to their implications for the LH surge, are not fully supported by the findings.' The editor notes that 'evidence for the conclusion that the findings explain how estradiol acts in the intact female were incomplete because they lacked experimental conditions that better approximate physiological conditions.' Reviewers emphasize that the OVX vs. OVX+E2 comparison does not reflect 'the physiological conditions under which the proposed transition...might take place.'
